about.title: Buena Park Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Buena Park trust the doctors, nurses, and clinics they see, and most of the time that trust is well placed. Medicine is hard, and a poor result by itself is not malpractice. The question that matters under California law is different: did a provider fall below the accepted standard of care, and did that failure cause real harm? Answering that almost always requires a qualified medical expert to review your records, which is one reason these cases move differently than a typical injury claim. Timing matters too. MICRA generally gives you one year from the date you discovered the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred, plus a 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit is filed. For Orange County residents juggling follow-up appointments along Beach Boulevard or a commute on SR-91, that clock can slip by quietly. We offer a free consultation to review your records and explain whether a claim makes sense.

whyChoose.title: Why Buena Park Residents Choose Us

items.title: MICRA's Deadlines Are Unforgiving
items.desc: California's one-year discovery rule, three-year outer limit, and 90-day pre-suit notice leave little margin. We can pin down your dates early so nothing is lost to the calendar.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Under MICRA, a qualified medical expert must generally confirm that care fell below the standard. Our team knows how to arrange that evaluation before anything is filed.

items.title: Free Consultation, Contingency Representation
items.desc: We offer a free initial review, and we work on contingency, meaning no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. Note that MICRA caps non-economic damages, and that cap rises each year.

items.question: My surgery in Orange County didn't go the way I expected. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law distinguishes between a known risk that materializes and a provider who fell below the accepted standard of care. A qualified medical expert typically has to review the records to make that call. We can arrange that review and give you an honest read on whether a claim is realistic.

items.question: How long do I have to act if I live in Buena Park?
items.answer: MICRA generally allows one year from the time you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from when the injury happened. Before filing suit, a 90-day notice of intent must be sent to the provider. Because these limits overlap, it is worth speaking with us as soon as you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: Yes, in part. MICRA places a cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, and that cap increases every year under the current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled separately. We can explain how these categories apply to your specific situation.
